architectural_units.name: Security Service
architectural_units.description: Security Service (Traefik) functions as a reverse proxy and load balancer, managing HTTP and HTTPS request routing.

architectural_units.name: Traefik
architectural_units.description: Traefik is a modern reverse proxy and load balancer designed to manage incoming and outgoing HTTP and HTTPS traffic in container-based applications.

architectural_units.name: System Service
architectural_units.description: System Service (Next.js) serves the web application using React and interacts with the database and external services.

architectural_units.name: Next.js
architectural_units.description: Next.js is a framework for building web applications that supports both client-side and server-side rendering.

architectural_units.name: Data Service
architectural_units.description: Data Service (PostgreSQL) provides the relational database for storing application data.

architectural_units.name: PostgreSQL
architectural_units.description: PostgreSQL is the relational database management system used to store application data.

architectural_units.name: Prisma
architectural_units.description: Prisma is an ORM tool used to simplify database access and management in Node.js and TypeScript applications.

architectural_units.name: Docker
architectural_units.description: Docker is a platform used to manage the execution of containers for the application services.
Security Service (Traefik) routes HTTP/HTTPS traffic to the System Service (Next.js).
System Service (Next.js) communicates with the Data Service (PostgreSQL) using Prisma.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The architecture implemented for the development of the Revivack project system is a microservices-based architecture.

patterns.name: Component-Based
patterns.description: The Component-Based pattern focuses on building the user interface by creating independent and reusable components.

patterns.name: Observer Pattern
patterns.description: The Observer pattern establishes a one-to-many relationship between objects, where the subject notifies observers of state changes.

patterns.name: Singleton Pattern
patterns.description: The Singleton pattern ensures that a class has only one instance and provides a global access point to that instance.
